q: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on earth glorify Allaah
(even though man may not perceive this),
v.s: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is exalting God, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
v.c: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth ˹constantly˺ glorifies Allah—the King, the Most Holy, the Almighty, the All-Wise.

q: It is He Who sent among the unlettered
purifies them and teaches them the Book
v.s: It is He who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from themselves reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] and wisdom [i.e., the sunnah] - although they were before in clear error -
v.c: He is the One Who raised for the illiterate ˹people˺ a messenger from among themselves—reciting to them His revelations, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, for indeed they had previously been clearly astray—

q: (Allaah had also sent Rasulullaah ﷺ as a Prophet to)
have not yet met. He is the Mighty, the Wise
(guides and uses for the propagation of His Deen whoever He wills, be they Arabs or non-Arabs).
v.s: And [to] others of them who have not yet joined them. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
v.c: along with others of them who have not yet joined them ˹in faith˺. For He is the Almighty, All-Wise.

q: (sending of Rasulullaah ﷺ to guide mankind))
is Allaah's grace which He grants to whoever He pleases
Allaah is the Possessor of immense grace.
v.s: That is the bounty of God, which He gives to whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty.
v.c: This is the favour of Allah. He grants it to whoever He wills. And Allah is the Lord of infinite bounty.

q: the Torah and then failed to bear it
is like that of a donkey carrying books.
(Despite being able to carry a wealth of knowledge on its back the donkey does not benefit from the knowledge.)
is the example of the people who reject Allaah's Aayaat. Allaah does not guide unjust
(The guidance Allaah sends is of no use to people who stubbornly reject the truth.)
v.s: The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not take it on is like that of a donkey who carries volumes [of books]. Wretched is the example of the people who deny the signs of God. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people.
v.c: The example of those who were entrusted with ˹observing˺ the Torah but failed to do so, is that of a donkey carrying books. How evil is the example of those who reject Allah’s signs! For Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.

q: (In reply to the claim of the Jews that only they are worthy of entering Jannah because they are Allaah's friends, Allaah says,)
that you are Allaah's friends and others are not, then wish
(so that you can reach Jannah quickly)
v.s: Say, "O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are allies of God, excluding the [other] people, then wish for death, if you should be truthful."
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O Jews! If you claim to be Allah’s chosen ˹people˺ out of all humanity, then wish for death, if what you say is true.”

q: They shall never wish for death because of the
(fear they have for the punishment due to them on account of the evil)
actions that their hands have sent forth. Allaah has
v.s: But they will not wish for it, ever, because of what their hands have put forth. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
v.c: But they will never wish for that because of what their hands have done. And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of the wrongdoers.

q: “Verily the death that you flee from shall certainly find you. Thereafter,
you shall be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the seen and He will inform
you of what you used to do.”
(Then you will have no escape from His punishment.)
v.s: Say, "Indeed, the death from which you flee - indeed, it will meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you about what you used to do."
v.c: Say, “The death you are running away from will inevitably come to you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the seen and unseen, and He will inform you of what you used to do.”

q: O you who have Imaan! When the call
salaah on the day of Jumu'ah
(towards the Jumu'ah salaah to take place in the Masjid)
and leave trading. This is best for you
(the eternal value of the salaah, which far exceeds the temporary value of the wealth you may attain from trading at that time).
v.s: O you who have believed, when [the adhān] is called for the prayer on the day of Jumuʿah [Friday], then proceed to the remembrance of God and leave trade. That is better for you, if you only knew.
v.c: O believers! When the call to prayer is made on Friday, then proceed ˹diligently˺ to the remembrance of Allah and leave off ˹your˺ business. That is best for you, if only you knew.

q: When the salaah has been completed then
in the land, seek from Allaah's bounty
(earn your living without suspending trade for the entire day as the Jews do on Saturdays)
(engage in Dhikr wherever you may be)
so that you may be successful
v.s: And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of God, and remember God often that you may succeed.
v.c: Once the prayer is over, disperse throughout the land and seek the bounty of Allah. And remember Allah often so you may be successful.

q: (The Sahabah ﵃ were listening to the Khutbah [sermon] being delivered by Rasulullaah ﷺ when a long- awaited caravan appeared in Madinah. There was a shortage of food in Madinah during that time and food prices were very high. Thinking that there was no harm in leaving before the Khutbah ended and fearing that the Jews and Munaafiqeen would get most of the merchandise, many of the Sahabah ﵃ hurried to meet the caravan without waiting for the Khutbah to end. Referring to this, Allaah says,)
they hurry to it and leave you
(where you are in the process of delivering the Friday Khutbah).
and trade. Allaah is the Best of providers.”
v.s: But [on one occasion] when they saw a transaction or a diversion, [O Muhammad], they rushed to it and left you standing. Say, “What is with God is better than diversion and than a transaction, and God is the best of providers.”
v.c: When they saw the fanfare along with the caravan, they ˹almost all˺ flocked to it, leaving you ˹O Prophet˺ standing ˹on the pulpit˺. Say, “What is with Allah is far better than amusement and merchandise. And Allah is the Best Provider.”
